reviewer: Codex: source review and executed acceptance evidence (not an independent reviewer)

adversarialFindings.description: A cursor can hide complete XP materialization or silently return a partial total on malformed rows.
adversarialFindings.resolution: The actual shared surface uses one validated XP cursor and a scalar accumulator. The first schema error is retained and thrown outside Dexie's callback wrapper. Access, scale and malformed-tail tests execute this path.

adversarialFindings.description: Separately read unlock and XP values could represent different committed states.
adversarialFindings.resolution: One readonly transaction covers exactly achievement_unlocks and xp_transactions; a barrier test blocks a competing two-store write and verifies coherent before/after results.

adversarialFindings.description: Persisted definitions, unrelated unlocks or retry composition could broaden the surface or alter semantics.
adversarialFindings.resolution: Code definitions remain authoritative, unlock access uses the existing unique achievementId index, and actual classic/RPG surface and independent child/HUD retry tests preserve labels, filtering, dates and zero passive writes.

adversarialFindings.description: The RPG route still scans XP once for the separate A4 HUD and once for the A6 child.
adversarialFindings.resolution: Explicitly allowed by the frozen A6 contract; both scans are visible in evidence and neither materializes complete XP history. Schema and ownership remain unchanged.

retrospective.summary: Proceed to native exact-commit certification only after full isolated precommit gates and exact-byte apply. Focused evidence includes a valid baseline RED and 18/18 corrected tests. One correction round separated a semantic-test selector recurrence from a real cursor validation defect. Native commands and review schema are used directly; local acceptance requires the generated release manifest to pass and bind this file's bytes. No remote publication is authorized.
